_meta.purpose: Phase 2 Tranche C part 3d, Stage 2 output: raw eval run results. NO analysis, NO threshold derivation performed on this data yet -- reserved for Stage 3.
_meta.corpus: 4 topics x 2 languages x 4 chunks = 32 chunks, agency 56fbfe38, seeded in 20260902130000_seed_knowledge_base_probe.sql
_meta.harness: supabase/functions/rag-eval-harness (commit 5ecd9ed) -- match_agency_knowledge called with _match_threshold: 0 (unfiltered), results collapsed to per-document best-chunk score via collapseToDocumentBest(), ALL documents returned per side (never top-k truncated).
_meta.fts_document_count_note: search_agency_knowledge hard-filters to chunks sharing at least one lexeme with the query (its zero-rows gate) -- fewer than 4 fts_documents for a question is expected/correct when vocabulary does not overlap at all, not missing data. semantic_documents is always 4/4 since cosine similarity is computable regardless of lexical overlap.
_meta.validation: All 38 questions returned zero harness errors and complete semantic_documents (4/4) on re-run after the merge-script fix; fts_documents document counts ranged 0-3 depending on lexical overlap, as expected.

questions.question: I can't make my shift, what do I do?
questions.rationale: RELABELED per review: primary intent reads as not attending at all (call-off), not as leaving a shift already in progress -- unlike q18/q20, it doesn't explicitly invoke both concepts, so labeling it ambiguous would presume the answer the eval is meant to measure. Labeled answerable-primary with pto_policy as an expected near-miss so Stage 2 measures the actual score gap between the two documents for this exact phrasing (the live-observed 3c near-miss) instead of assuming ambiguity a priori. A small measured gap becomes evidence for a disambiguation trigger; a large gap confirms this is retrieval imprecision, not genuine ambiguity.
